# True north statement

The ideal, not-fully-reachable direction behind a Hoshin plan, broken into its real component pillars and checked against whether current work actually traces back to each one — with any pillar nobody's moving toward flagged plainly, not smoothed over.

Family: Hoshin Kanri · Format: .xlsx · Domain: core

## What it is

A true north statement is a real, checkable answer to 'is this direction actually connected to real work, or is it just a mission-statement sentence' — True North (Lean Enterprise Institute, Art of Lean) is the ideal, deliberately not-fully-reachable direction an organization points toward, genuinely distinct from a Hoshin annual objective's this-year reachable target. This statement breaks that single sentence into a fixed set of pillars, then checks a flat list of current initiatives against them: which pillars have real, committed work tracing to them, which have nothing at all, and which logged initiatives are only floated ideas nobody's actually committed resources to yet.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- A Hoshin X-Matrix already exists (or a stated mission/direction does) and you want to check honestly whether this year's real work actually traces back to it, pillar by pillar.
- You suspect the organization's stated direction has drifted from what people are actually working on, and you want that gap named plainly rather than assumed closed.
- You want to know which component of your direction has zero real initiatives behind it, not just which projects feel aligned in general.

Not when:

- You don't have any real direction stated yet — this statement checks work against a direction that already exists, it doesn't invent one.
- You're setting this year's specific targets and strategies — that's the Hoshin X-Matrix itself; this statement sits above it, checking the X-Matrix's own trueNorth field against reality.

## How to fill it in

- **trueNorthNotes** — In one or two sentences, what's the ideal, not-fully-reachable direction this points toward?
- **pillars** — Break that direction into its real component pillars, even ones you expect have no work behind them yet.
- **initiatives** — For each initiative: which pillar it's tagged to, an owner, and — if it's real committed work, not just a floated idea — which annual objective or strategy it actually traces back to.
- **narrative** — Drafted from the statement's own computed coverage.

## What good looks like

The example below expands Northwind Fabrication's already-published FY2027 Hoshin plan's own trueNorth field into four real pillars, checks each against that plan's already-committed annual objectives and strategies, and finds one pillar with nothing tracing to it at all — every current strategy serves customers already calling, none reach the ones who aren't yet.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://www.katafacts.com/katas/true-north-statement

## Common mistakes

- **Writing pillars that just restate this year's annual objectives with different words.** — A pillar is the ideal direction an objective should trace back to, not a rename of the objective itself — if a pillar and an annual objective say the same thing, the pillar isn't doing its own job.
- **Counting a floated idea as covering a pillar because it's tagged to the right one.** — An initiative with no real linked objective is an aspiration, not committed work — this statement flags it as unlinked specifically so it can't be mistaken for a pillar that's actually being moved on.
- **Leaving a pillar out because you already suspect nothing traces to it.** — An unlisted pillar can't be flagged as disconnected — naming it and letting it come up with zero initiatives is exactly how this tool surfaces the gap plainly instead of hiding it by omission.

## What it connects to

Upstream:

- **Hoshin Kanri — X-Matrix** — The X-Matrix's own trueNorth field is exactly the sentence this statement expands into pillars, and its annual objectives/strategies are the real, committed work each pillar is checked against.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding whether an initiative genuinely traces back to a real commitment or is still just a floated idea
- Deciding which disconnected pillar to raise at the next catchball round

Analysis — AI helps:

- Tightening an initiative's wording from rough notes into a specific, checkable statement
- Drafting the narrative from the statement's own computed coverage

Drudgery — automated:

- Identifying which pillars have no initiatives logged
- Identifying which logged initiatives are still unlinked
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
